properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped library surface for the geth console JS runtime; the web3.js application code itself only invokes the SHA3/keccak module, so RC4 ships unused — but present in every released binary. RC4 is broken classically (not a PQ issue); must never be wired to data. Changeable here by replacing the vendored bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped library surface; no application call site found. 3DES has a 64-bit block (Sweet32) and is NIST-disallowed; ships unused in every binary. Changeable here by replacing the vendored bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped library surface; no application call site found (console web3.js only uses the SHA3 module). MD5 collisions make HMAC-MD5 a deprecated MAC; it ships unused. Same remediation path as RC4/3DES: replace the vendored bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The core cryptographic asset of this codebase (celo-blockchain, a go-ethereum fork): ECDSA over secp256k1 signs every account key and transaction, identifies p2p nodes (ENR), and backs the RLPx/discv4/discv5 handshakes via the ecies package. Shor-vulnerable: every ECDSA signature and public key ever published on-chain is harvestable. No PQ account scheme is deployed; replacing it requires an ecosystem/protocol migration (account abstraction with ML-DSA/SLH-DSA or hybrid), changeable only via a c

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Posture control, rating C: comparisons of digests with == across the codebase. Overwhelmingly public chain data (block/tx hashes) where a timing side-channel is not security-relevant; no secret-MAC == comparison surfaced in the sample — the keystore MAC check itself uses bytes.Equal (see the constant-time comparison object). Two non-digest false matches rejected at site level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Confirmed as weak-PRNG surface present in the shipped binary; no exploitable use found — the security-relevant randomness all comes from crypto/rand (the CSPRNG object), so this is a posture note, not a defect.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CTR (128-bit) without built-in authentication: geth keystore v3 (aes-128-ctr + separate Keccak MAC), legacy presale wallets, ECIES message encryption, discv5 who-are-you auth-header masking, RLPx frame encryption. CTR malleability is mitigated by MACs layered in each protocol; CNSA 2.0 would want AES-256-GCM. First-party, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA account/node key generation: accounts/keystore/key.go NewKey, crypto/crypto.go GenerateKey, plus test keygen. Same logical asset as the ECDSA object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Legacy pre-sale wallet format (2014): AES-128-CBC with PKCS#7, key from PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(pass, pass, 2000) — decrypt-only compatibility code for importing old wallets. Unauthenticated CBC, but the format is fixed by the historical files themselves.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JS-side wallet crypto (secp256k1 signing/address derivation) for the ethers.js e2e tests; mirrors the Go-side secp256k1 object ALG-673c8f24. Test-scope, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA-over-secp256k1 is the node's signature primitive: account keys (keystore), transaction and istanbul consensus-message signing, p2p node identity, devp2p DNSSEC validation. Shor-vulnerable; migration to ML-DSA would require chain-coordinated protocol changes rather than a library swap. Primitive-level view also held by ALG-673c8f24 (secp256k1).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Standalone ECDH — the highest-value harvest-now-decrypt-later class here since devp2p traffic is passively capturable. Migration target ML-KEM-768 hybrid, but RLPx/discv5 schemes are protocol-fixed: changeable only via devp2p protocol revision coordinated network-wide.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Standard-curve ECIES parameter sets shipped in the library; production use of ecies here is on secp256k1 (RLPx). P-256 ECDH/ECDSA is Shor-vulnerable; ML-KEM-768 replaces its key-agreement role. Presence in the shipped library is the inventory fact even without a production call site.

components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.19)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The tree's only TLS posture: default Go crypto/tls (TLS 1.2/1.3), ECDHE-only key exchange, no post-quantum group offered; Go 1.24+ would offer X25519MLKEM768 by default. Sessions harvestable today (librato telemetry, incl. basic-auth credentials). Two of the three detector hits never open a TLS session — rejected at site level. No InsecureSkipVerify and no custom cipher/group lists anywhere in first-party Go code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The runtime libraries ship Ed25519 arithmetic (also via filippo.io/edwards25519 indirect dep); the algorithm's live use sites are covered by the ALG-5e08bdf5 object. Dependency-inventory confirmation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: A posture control, not a weakness: crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare defends the ECIES decrypt MAC check against timing side channels — the correct implementation. Its presence documents that the ecies MAC path is timing-safe.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Standard-curve ECIES parameter sets (ECIES_AES256_SHA384 for P-384, P-521 variants) shipped in the library; production ecies use here is on secp256k1 (RLPx). P-384/P-521 are Shor-vulnerable; ML-KEM-768 replaces the key-agreement role. Library surface confirmed present and tested.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Supplementary reading of site accounts/keystore/passphrase.go:288-289: this Keccak-256 call computes the v3 keystore integrity MAC (over the KDF-derived key half + ciphertext); line 289 then compares it to the stored MAC with bytes.Equal — non-constant-time, unlike the ECIES tag check which uses subtle.ConstantTimeCompare (crypto/ecies/ecies.go:312). Posture note (CWE-208) for a later constant-time hardening pass; the MAC computation itself is the SHA-3 asset recorded here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 is the keystore's cipher (16-byte scrypt/PBKDF2-derived key) and ECIES's default message cipher (ECIES_AES128_SHA256 for both secp256k1 and P-256). Grover leaves ~64-bit quantum margin — acceptable but below CNSA 2.0's AES-256 floor. Test vectors document the on-disk format.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Memory-hard KDF protecting keystore v3 keys: standard N=2^18 (r=8, p=1, dkLen=32), with a --lightkdf N=2^12 relaxation for constrained use (cmd/ethkey). Quantum-irrelevant. very-light-scrypt.json is a deliberately weak test fixture for the format.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 in CTR mode appears in protocol-fixed places: legacy presale wallet decryption (AES-128-CTR/CBC from PBKDF2-SHA256-2000), discv5 challenge masking (encoding.go:637 uses destID[:16] as key — specified by the discv5 protocol), RLPx frame encryption/MAC (rlpx.go:326/330 — AES-128-CTR per devp2p spec), discv5 session AES, and signer AES-GCM storage. Symmetric AES-128 is Grover-halved to 64-bit-equivalent but not Shor-broken; the harvestable part is the ECDH feeding it (covered by the ECDH ob

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AEAD uses: discv5 packet encryption (AES-GCM over HKDF-derived session keys, protocol-fixed) and the signer's encrypted credential storage (AES-256-GCM per the AES-256 object's tests). AES-GCM is PQ-neutral apart from key size; the harvestable secret is the secp256k1 ECDH beneath discv5 (see ECDH object). Storage-side GCM is the correct modern choice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js HMAC helpers (SHA-256/384/512) vendored in the web3.js bundle — shipped library surface, no application call site; sound MAC constructions. The 2 fourbyte-database string sites are rejected per-site below.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: discv5 (Node Discovery Protocol v5) derives all session keys via HKDF-SHA256 from the secp256k1 ECDH secret — a proper KDF in a Shor-vulnerable handshake. The harvestable asset is the traffic (HNDL) via the underlying ECDH; HKDF itself is PQ-neutral. Protocol-fixed; changeable via discv5 revision.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The X9.63 Concat KDF derives the AES/MAC keys from the ECDH shared point in ECIES — the geth RLPx handshake encryption (p2p/rlpx) and the shipped ecies library. The KDF itself is a symmetric construction (PQ-neutral); the Shor exposure is the secp256k1 ECDH feeding it. Standard for ECIES (IEEE 1363a / ANSI X9.63).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 from both toolchains: x/crypto/sha3 backs the Keccak-256 consensus hash and SHAKE256 consensus randomness (Go), @noble/hashes backs the ethers.js e2e harness (JS). Quantum-safe family, low urgency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Consensus-critical: SHAKE256 XOF drives the Fisher-Yates validator-set permutation (consensus/istanbul/validator/random). Deterministic by design — all validators derive the same ordering from the epoch seed; randomness quality rests on the seed, not the PRNG. Provided by golang.org/x/crypto/sha3; quantum-safe.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hash dependency of the ethers.js e2e test harness; SHA-256 is quantum-safe. Test-scope.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 availability in the JS e2e harness's hash library; no first-party call site found. Test-scope dependency.

properties.value: Available in the shipped x/crypto/sha3; no first-party SHAKE128 call site found — SHAKE256 is the variant actually used (validator ordering, ALG-6d9e0af5). Presence-level entry for the shipped library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Release-integrity manifest for distributed artifacts — governance artifact, regenerated per release. SHA-256 is quantum-safe; artifact-verification use only.

properties.name: pqs:context

SHA-2-512 family is PQ-neutral (Grover only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 surfaces: the ECIES AES256 parameter sets (library), and the signer's AES-256-GCM credential storage (aes_gcm_storage.go — derived from a passphrase via the keystore-grade KDF). 256-bit keys are Grover-comfortable; this is the strong end of the symmetric inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHAKE256: declared via go.mod and live at consensus/istanbul/validator/random:27 (validator-ordering PRNG). Quantum-safe XOF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The good-side counterpart of the non-cryptographic PRNG object; together they give the codebase's randomness posture. Go's crypto/rand reads the OS CSPRNG — quantum-safe in practice (only Grover's quadratic speedup applies to the underlying primitives, compensated by 256-bit entropy).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The project's primary external crypto dependency: scrypt+PBKDF2 for the keystore KDF, HKDF for discv5, SHA3/Keccak for everything, ripemd160 for the EVM precompile, openpgp for release signing, ed25519 support. Version matters for PQ capability: v0.21.0 predates Go's crypto/mlkem — this dependency tree offers no post-quantum algorithms; TLS-level PQ (X25519MLKEM768) requires Go 1.24+. Changeable here (dependency bump).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hash library of the ethers.js e2e test harness (SHA-256, SHA-3/Keccak, BLAKE3 entries). Test-scope dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve library of the ethers.js e2e test harness (secp256k1, P-256, Ed25519 entries). Test-scope dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency: archived jwt-go v3.2.0+incompatible (CVE-2020-26160 aud-claim bypass; predates modern alg hardening). No first-party JWT use in this tree. Recorded for dependency hygiene; same logical asset as LIB-1d84a23e.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Version pin is the PQ-relevant fact: x/crypto v0.21.0 (and the go 1.19 toolchain) provide no post-quantum primitives, so every classical asymmetric use in this repo has no in-tree PQ fallback. Changeable here via dependency/toolchain bump.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Release signing tooling (build-time only, not shipped in the node binary). The signing key's algorithm (RSA vs EdDSA) is set by the external armored key, undeclared in-repo. golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is frozen/deprecated since 2020; release-signing is a Shor-deadline risk and the signer should move to a maintained implementation (minisign/Ed25519 is already used elsewhere in this tree for version-check). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed test credential: a well-known secp256k1 test-account key used by cmd/geth account-import tests. Test-only but real key material in version control — the key and its address must be treated as public.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The KDF library behind keystore v3 key encryption; current x/crypto line, PQ-safe.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive module-graph requirement of archived jwt-go v3.2.0 — not built into the node. Vulnerable line (CVE-2020-26160) noted for dependency hygiene. Same logical asset as ALG-240215d0 (JWT signing).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The keystore's scrypt-era sibling KDF: v1 keystore files derive their AES key via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (passphrase.go:374), and the legacy presale wallet via PBKDF2-SHA256 with 2000 iterations (below OWASP minimum — protocol-frozen file format; noted in the SHA-256 object's context). PBKDF2 itself is PQ-neutral.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve25519/Ed25519 field-arithmetic library pinned to a 2020 pre-release alpha — a dependency-hygiene note rather than a weak algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF over the discv5 ECDH secret — sound KDF in a Shor-vulnerable handshake (see ECDH/HKDF objects for the full story).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x/crypto/openpgp is frozen/deprecated upstream (no maintenance since 2017; SHA-1 key IDs, RSA/ElGamal era design) — flagged as an outstanding defect independent of PQ. Its live use is being filed as a separate finding (internal/build/pgp.go: ArmoredDetachSign). Changeable here by migrating release signing to signify/minisign (already used for version checks) or a maintained PGP library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is the hashing backbone of the entire chain: addresses, tx/block hashes, the Merkle Patricia trie, RLPx MAC (keccak-secret), and the SHA3 EVM precompile family. SHA-3 is PQ-neutral (Grover only). The SHA-3/Keccak algorithm objects in the inventory rest on this dependency.
